correctness.rationale: The explicit midpoint condition for a factor containing both marked ones is equivalent to the parity condition and |i-j| <= b. Unary factors and one-marked factors are handled exhaustively. The diagonal sum counts each distinct string exactly once. Continuum overlap area has an exact triangle-subtraction formula; the mesh-two diagonal sum differs from half the area by O(n) uniformly. Exhaustive cases prove the sharp area bound s^2/8 with sole equality proportions (3/8,1/4,3/8). Compactness proves the iff rigidity. The extracted standalone verifier checked exact factor-set equality in 2197 triples and two 25-parameter closed specializations. Unbounded correctness relies on proof, not enumerations.

originality.rationale: The equal-run construction of Fici et al. is a special lower-bound witness, while Simpson gives a different explicit one-parameter asymmetric specialization. The newly asserted scope is every binary word with exactly two marked letters, the exact factor set, optimized sharp constant 1/16, and its unique asymptotic run-ratio. No inspected primary work or returned published-record summary established all these assertions. This is a best-knowledge assessment with named source-access risk, not a uniqueness proof.
residual_risks: The full primary text of Kociumaka et al. 2016 was inaccessible; the available abstract and Simpson 2018 discussion are insufficient to exclude an exact specialization definitively.
Semantic and web searches cannot establish absolute novelty; a differently named or unindexed two-marker optimization may exist.

value.rationale: Two rare markers are the first binary sparse-symbol class permitting quadratically many distinct Abelian-square factors; zero or one marker gives only unary Abelian squares. The complete classification describes every factor, and the sharp constant and unique limit shape optimize the historically important sparse witness, improving the equal-run 1/18 coefficient to 1/16. This is a natural infinite-family extremal result rather than an arbitrary finite parameter, and it does not need an invented downstream application.
